rationale: The plan correctly recognizes n=1 per group, refuses any Wald/LRT test, p-values, FDR or shrinkage, reports median-of-ratios normalized counts with descriptive log2FC, sets control as the reference, and names the replicated design (>=3 per group) needed for inference; the report section is thorough with versions, gene counts, caveats and session info. QC is appropriate for two samples (library sizes, vst PCA, distances) with an explicit no-silent-drop policy, and the >=10-counts-in->=1-sample filter is justified by group size. The main weakness is Step 3: enrichment is not warranted on an n=1 fold-change ranking, and fgsea inherently emits set-level p-values/padj, which sits uneasily with the reference's 'no p-values' stance even though the plan labels it descriptive; the plan should have omitted it rather than running it with caveats.
